channel.title: Coastal Eventures: upcoming events
channel.description: The next 40 dated events on the Gulf Coast.

item.title: Elevate Relationship Workshop at the Fort Walton Beach Library (WED 11/4)
item.description: Friday 10/30 · 6:00 PM · Saturday 10/31 · 9:00 AM · Saturday 11/7 · 9:00 AM | Fort Walton Beach Library | No published price. Healthy Relationships Emerald Coast returns to the Fort Walton Beach Library with a three-day Elevate Relationship Workshop for adults. Sessions run Friday October 30 from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM, Saturday October 31 from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM and Saturday November 7 from 9:00 AM to 1:30 PM. Lunch is provided on November 7.

item.title: Foo Foo Festival (WED 11/4)
item.description: Thu 10/29 to Mon 11/9 | Downtown Pensacola | No published price. Foo Foo Festival runs across downtown Pensacola from October 29 through November 9, one of the destination's own signature annual events. Visit Pensacola's page for it doesn't spell out a program, since it covers many venues under one banner.

item.title: Greater Gulf State Fair (WED 11/4)
item.description: Oct 30 to Nov 8 · Weekdays 4 PM · Weekends 12 PM | Greater Gulf State Fairgrounds | No published price. The Greater Gulf State Fair fills the Mobile fairgrounds for ten days with a midway of rides, a rodeo, a community stage and a pickin porch. It is the largest fair in the Mobile area and a good outing for a family that wants a full evening of rides and fair food. Children 4 and under do not need an admission ticket, though they do need a wristband to ride. General admission and ride prices are not printed on the fair's pages, so check the ticket store before driving over.

item.title: Jazz Art Writers South Festival Youth Exhibit 2026 (WED 11/4)
item.description: Nov 1 to Dec 15 · all day during branch hours, closed Sundays | Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library | No published price. More than fifty paintings by artists ages 8 to 18 who attend local public schools interpret jazz music at the Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library. The JAWS Festival put the exhibit together with the Mobile Arts Council and the Amp Up Arts Program, and it hangs from November 1 through December 15 during branch hours, which are Monday to Saturday.

item.title: Lightspill (mirrored-sphere art installation) (WED 11/4)
item.description: Thursday 10/29 to Monday 11/9 · times not posted | Artel Gallery | Free. Lightspill is a large temporary public art installation by Friends of Downtown on the front of the historic Artel Gallery building in downtown Pensacola. Hundreds of mirrored spheres appear to pour over the facade, and the look changes through the day with light and weather. It's free and open to the public, from October 29 to November 9, as part of Foo Foo Festival.

item.title: Make Your Own Glass (hot glass, by appointment) (WED 11/4)
item.description: By appointment: Wednesdays 5 PM-9 PM, Saturdays 8 AM-11 AM | First City Art Center | from $85. Make Your Own Glass is a hands-on hot glass session at First City Art Center in Pensacola, where each participant makes a piece with a glassblower. It's for ages 8 and up including adults, by appointment on Wednesdays from 5-9 PM and Saturdays from 8-11 AM. The finished piece cools in an annealing oven and is picked up the following week. Standard pieces cost $85, and premium pieces such as a pumpkin, ornament, cup or bowl cost $110-$140.

item.title: Mobile in the Gilded Age exhibition at the History Museum of Mobile (WED 11/4)
item.description: Monday to Saturday 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM · Sunday 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM · through 6/6/2027 | History Museum of Mobile | from $8. The History Museum of Mobile opened Mobile in the Gilded Age on October 9, 2026, and the exhibition stays up through June 6, 2027. Gowns, inventions and everyday objects show how railroads, new technology and department stores changed life in Mobile in the late 1800s and early 1900s. The exhibition also covers the unequal opportunities and segregation of the period.

item.title: Mobile Music Legends exhibit at Moorer Branch Library (WED 11/4)
item.description: Library hours · 11/1 to 12/15 · closed Sundays | Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library | No published price. The Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library hosts the first annual Mobile Music Legends exhibit. The display celebrates artists and ensembles who carried the soul, jazz and spirit of the Gulf Coast to the world. The exhibit stays up from November 1 to December 15.

item.title: Night Moves Music Fest (WED 11/4)
item.description: Thursday 10/29 to Sunday 11/8 · times vary by show | The Handlebar, Lagunas, Odd Colony, Betty's and more | No published price. Night Moves is a multi-venue music festival across Pensacola for eleven days, covering indie and alternative, punk, EDM and singer-songwriter shows. Venues named include The Handlebar, Lagunas, Odd Colony and Betty's. Individual shows at The Handlebar are listed as all ages at $20 to $25, with doors at 6 PM and music at 7 PM.

item.title: Painting with a Twist Pensacola: paint-and-sip, family paint days and date nights (weekly programme) (WED 11/4)
item.description: Classes most days: family days Saturday 10:30 AM, brunch Sunday 11 AM, evenings Wednesday to Saturday | Painting with a Twist Pensacola | $35 per family. Painting with a Twist Pensacola is an artist-led paint-and-sip studio at 4771 Bayou Blvd Suite C11 with several classes every week. October has family paint days (ages 6 and up with a parent, no alcohol), adult Paint & Sip and Date Night classes (ages 16 and up on date nights), Halloween-themed canvases and Paint Your Pet. Classes cost $35-$60 depending on the class, and alcohol is sold on site with no BYOB.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Yoga: Friday and Wednesday beach classes (WED 11/4)
item.description: Fridays 9 AM and Wednesdays 6 PM | Pensacola Beach Yoga, beside the Gulf Pier | from $10. Pensacola Beach Yoga runs drop-in yoga on the sand beside the Gulf Pier at 41 Fort Pickens Road in Pensacola Beach. Classes are Fridays at 9 AM and Wednesdays at 6 PM, and they cost $10 with no registration. Bring a mat or towel.

item.title: Public Ice Skating at the Pensacola Bay Center, November sessions (WED 11/4)
item.description: Nov 1 to Nov 25 · one hour sessions, see dates | Pensacola Bay Center | from $15. The Pensacola Bay Center opens its ice for one-hour public skate sessions. The November sessions run Sunday 11/1 at 6:30 PM, Saturday 11/7 and Sunday 11/8 at 1:30, 3:00 and 4:30 PM, Friday 11/13 and Saturday 11/14 at 9:30 PM, Sunday 11/15 at 1:30, 3:00 and 4:30 PM, and Wednesday 11/25 at 9:30 PM. The Bay Center states that all sessions are subject to change.

item.title: Science on the Street (sound and music science) (WED 11/4)
item.description: Thursday 10/29 to Sunday 11/8 · Sound Booth Fri 10/30 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM, Sun 11/1 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM, Sat 11/7 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM | Palafox Street between Garden and Main | Free. Science on the Street is a self-guided, hands-on look at the science of sound on Palafox Street between Garden and Main in Pensacola, from October 29 to November 8. It has oversized instruments, tuning forks, sound-wave displays and acoustics demonstrations. The Pensacola MESS Hall runs it as part of Foo Foo Festival, and it's free.

item.title: Side Show (musical, PenArts) (WED 11/4)
item.description: Friday 10/30 7:30 PM · Sunday 11/1 2:30 PM · Tuesday 11/3 to Saturday 11/7 7:30 PM · Sunday 11/8 2:30 PM (SOLD OUT) | The Gordon Community Art Center | from $20. Side Show is a musical staged by PenArts at The Gordon Community Art Center in Pensacola, about conjoined twins who became vaudeville stars. It plays Friday, October 30 through Sunday, November 8, with 7:30 PM evening shows and 2:30 PM Sunday matinees, and the Sunday, November 8 matinee is sold out. It suits elementary-school ages and up. Free outdoor attractions run before each show outside the venue. Tickets are $20.

item.title: The View Within exhibition at Blue Morning Gallery (WED 11/4)
item.description: Sunday 10/25 to Saturday 11/28 · reception Friday 11/6 at 4:30 | Blue Morning Gallery | No published price. Blue Morning Gallery in downtown Pensacola shows The View Within, an exhibition of colorful abstract paintings by the featured artist, from October 25 through November 28. A reception on Friday November 6 at 4:30 lets visitors meet the artist, hear live music and enjoy refreshments and conversation.

item.title: Wanda Sullivan: Bloem Exhibition (WED 11/4)
item.description: Now through December 11 | Anna Lamar Switzer Center for Visual Arts | No published price. A gallery exhibition by artist Wanda Sullivan runs at Pensacola State College's visual arts center through mid-December. The center's own site does not publish an admission price.

item.title: The Great Bellingrath Harvest (WED 11/4)
item.description: Daily through 11/8 · 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM | Bellingrath Gardens and Home | from $11. Bellingrath Gardens and Home runs a fall festival from September 19 through November 8 with seasonal displays across the gardens, including the scarecrow exhibit and pumpkin displays. The gardens are open daily, and the general admission price applies. The events page does not list a separate price for the harvest, so the gardens ticket is the number to plan with.

item.title: Shape & Sculpt Fitness Class (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 8:15 AM to 9:15 AM | Destin Community Center | from $5. Shape & Sculpt is a light-weight fitness class set to music at the Destin Community Center, built around muscle strength, balance and core work. The city says it's open to all ages and fitness levels, and it runs every Wednesday morning. Each class costs $5.

item.title: Cornhole Open Play (WED 11/4)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Members toss bags at the boards during open-play cornhole at the Niceville Senior Center. It runs casually throughout the center's regular weekday hours. City of Niceville residents play free, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Exercise Room (WED 11/4)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. The Niceville Senior Center's exercise room stays open for members to work through strength, cardio, and flexibility routines on their own schedule. Equipment includes two recumbent bikes, a treadmill, free weights, a stability ball, mats, and stretch bands. City of Niceville residents get free access, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Putting Green Open Play (WED 11/4)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Members check out putters and balls at the front desk to practice on the Niceville Senior Center's putting green. It is casual, and you can work on your short game alone or play a round with friends. City of Niceville residents get free access, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Table Tennis Open Play (WED 11/4)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. Niceville Senior Center's table tennis room is open for casual, drop-in play with no experience required. The city describes it as an active, social way to spend the morning rather than a competitive league. It shares the Tuesday 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM window with several other open-play programs at the center, and members age 55 and up are the intended audience.

item.title: Zumba Gold: Wednesday (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 8:30 AM to 9:30 AM | Niceville Senior Center | from $3. This Wednesday session of Zumba Gold is a low-impact class built around routines that are easy to follow. It asks a $3 donation and runs early, from 8:30 AM to 9:30 AM, at the Niceville Senior Center. It repeats weekly and is aimed at the center's members age 55 and up.

item.title: Plein Air Fairhope (WED 11/4)
item.description: Mon 11/2 to Fri 11/6 · painting sunrise to sunset · Fri 11/6 reception 6:00 PM · Sat 11/7 Quick Draw 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM | Eastern Shore Art Center and downtown Fairhope | Free. About 60 artists paint outdoors around downtown Fairhope and the pier from sunrise to sunset all week, and anyone can stop and watch. The free First Friday reception on November 6 has live music and opens the exhibition, which stays up through December 19. The Saturday Quick Draw welcomes all ages, and the only paid part is a $15 Gallery Talk with judge Cory Wright on Wednesday.

item.title: Veterans Chat 'n Chew (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Veterans gather at the Niceville Senior Center for an hour of casual conversation about the present and the past. The city describes it simply as a chance to get together with other veterans who share the experience. Access follows the center's usual membership rules, so residents attend free and others pay the standard day rate.

item.title: Beginner Line Dance: Wednesday (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 9:30 AM to 10:30 AM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. This beginner line dance class teaches simple steps for members new to the form. Because the sessions run crowded, the city asks participants to pick either the Wednesday or the Friday class rather than attending both. It meets from 9:30 AM to 10:30 AM at the Niceville Senior Center every Wednesday in November, on the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th.

item.title: Ping Pong Meet-Up (WED 11/4)
item.description: 9:30 AM to 11:00 AM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. This ping pong meetup at the Niceville Senior Center is open to beginners and experienced players alike, and the city says no experience is required to join in. It runs Wednesday mid morning and repeats on multiple weekdays.

item.title: Ages 3 to 5 Storytime Class at Crestview Library (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays or Thursdays · 10:00 AM | Crestview Library: Story Room | No published price. Crestview Library holds a weekly storytime class for preschoolers, with families choosing either the Wednesday or the Thursday session at 10:00 AM. Each class has stories, music, movement and a craft around a theme, such as Bugs on November 4 or 5, Kindness on November 12 and Octopus on November 18 or 19. Younger siblings and older children are welcome.

item.title: Aminah Robinson: Journeys Home at the Mobile Museum of Art (WED 11/4)
item.description: Tuesday to Saturday · 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM · through 1/9 | Mobile Museum of Art | from $8. Aminah Robinson: Journeys Home is a special exhibition at the Mobile Museum of Art that draws on the artist's historical research, folklore and personal narrative. The museum describes it as a visual memoir of her life and a tableau of the African American experience. It stays open through January 9, 2027.

item.title: Driven to Draw Tuesday morning drawing class at the Mobile Museum of Art (WED 11/4)
item.description: Tuesdays · 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM · 11/3, 11/10, 11/17 and 11/24 | Mobile Museum of Art | from $180. This four-week morning drawing class at the Mobile Museum of Art covers essential drawing techniques, playful exploration and confidence building. The museum welcomes beginners and people refining their skills, with supportive guidance in a relaxed room. Classes meet on four Tuesdays in November.

item.title: Gateway: From Graffiti to Gallery at the Mobile Museum of Art (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesday to Saturday · 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, through 9/1/2027 | Mobile Museum of Art | from $8. The Mobile Museum of Art traces how artists who started with graffiti in New York's subways moved into galleries, with work by Basquiat, Haring, Scharf, KAWS and Banksy from the Masterworks Foundation collection. The show runs a full year, Wednesday through Saturday. Mobile County residents get in free on Thursdays.

item.title: Good Listener Storytime at Moorer (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM | Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library | No published price. Young children gather at the Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library for stories, songs and early literacy activities in this half-hour storytime. It is also offered again on Wednesdays, including November 4, November 18 and November 25.

item.title: Handle with Care at the Mobile Museum of Art (WED 11/4)
item.description: Tuesday to Saturday · 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM · through 3/27 | Mobile Museum of Art | from $8. Handle with Care is an interactive special exhibition at the Mobile Museum of Art. Artists Calder Kamin of Austin and Jacob Reptile of New Orleans turn trash into soft, complex sculptures that visitors move through as an environment. It stays open through March 27, 2027.

item.title: Make It Last: Gallery Exhibition at UWF (WED 11/4)
item.description: Weekdays through 11/20 · 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM | UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts, Building 82, The Art Gallery | Free. Make It Last is an exhibition in The Art Gallery at the UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts, curated by a UWF graduate. Six artists share the space, which includes a conversation pit in the gallery alcove and a poetry wall that visitors fill with their own work. Admission is free.

item.title: Mexican Train Dominoes (WED 11/4)
item.description: 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. Mexican Train Dominoes at the Niceville Senior Center is pitched as easy to learn, welcoming first-time players alongside the regulars. It runs Wednesday late morning into early afternoon and repeats on multiple weekdays.

item.title: Shake, Rattle, & Read Storytime at West (WED 11/4)
item.description: 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM | West Regional Library | No published price. West Regional Library's Shake, Rattle, & Read Storytime pairs books with music and movement for young children and their caregivers. The library frames it as a chance for little ones to read, move, and build early literacy skills together. The library lists it every Wednesday and Thursday morning in the West Regional meeting room.

item.title: Story Time Shuffle at Foley Community Library (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:00 AM | Foley Community Library | No published price. Story Time Shuffle meets every Wednesday at 10:00 AM at the Foley Community Library from August through May. The format rotates by week: the first Wednesday is story time with Ms. Jo, the second adds music, the third is bilingual and the fourth is a puppet show. The next session is Wednesday November 4. The children's page prints no age limit or price.

item.title: The Naughty List Storytime with Maggie and Rosalind Bunn (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesday 11/4 · 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM | Page & Palette | No published price. Authors Maggie and Rosalind Bunn read their children's book The Naughty List at Page & Palette. The story follows a boy who wants onto Santa's Nice List and gets a Thanksgiving visit from Santa. The authors meet families and sign books afterward.

item.title: Timeless Hats by Susie Mae Pugh-Williams at the Mobile Museum of Art (WED 11/4)
item.description: Tuesday to Saturday · 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM · through 1/30 | Mobile Museum of Art | from $8. Timeless Hats is a special exhibition of more than two dozen hats at the Mobile Museum of Art. Some were made by Mrs. Williams, and others are hats she admired and drew inspiration from for her own creations. It stays open through January 30, 2027.

item.title: Wonderful Wednesday Storytime at Theodore (WED 11/4)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:00 AM | Theodore Oaks Branch Library | No published price. Theodore Oaks Branch Library's Wonderful Wednesday Storytime introduces young children to books, rhymes and music in the children's area. The program is built for preschoolers up to age 5, though all ages are welcome. Space is limited and seats go first come, first served.
